entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Gobryas, a distinguished Persian nobleman who died around 500 BCE, was a pivotal figure in the consolidation of the Achaemenid Empire under Darius I, particularly through his decisive role in the political crisis of 522 BCE. As one of the 'Seven' conspirators, he was instrumental in the overthrow of the usurper Gaumata, who falsely claimed the throne as Bardiya (Smerdis), preventing a potential period of fragmentation following the death of Cambyses II. His deep loyalty and military prowess positioned him as a trusted confidant and high-ranking official, serving notably as Darius's personal *arštibara*, or lance-bearer, a position of immense honor and proximity to the Great King, signifying his integral place within the nascent imperial structure.

The core of Gobryas's historical actions centers on the dramatic events of September 522 BCE. Alongside Darius and five other Persian magnates, he participated in the daring assassination of Gaumata at the fortress of Sikayauvati, an act vividly recounted in Darius's Behistun Inscription. This bold maneuver paved the way for Darius's ascension to the Achaemenid throne, effectively re-establishing stability after a period of widespread revolts. Gobryas's influence extended beyond this coup; he reportedly advised Darius during the subsequent campaigns to quell rebellions across the empire, and his presence is suggested in the Scythian campaign, further solidifying the empire's northern frontiers.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Gobryas's pivotal role in the overthrow of the usurper Gaumata directly secured Darius I's ascension to the Achaemenid throne, thereby stabilizing the empire and ensuring its continuity for centuries. His family's subsequent influence, particularly through his son Mardonius, left a lasting mark on Persian military and political history.
